events.label: US/Israel strike Iran
events.description: Surprise 12-hour campaign: ~900 strikes across 26 provinces. Khamenei and 7+ senior officials killed. Nuclear facilities at Natanz and Fordow hit.

events.label: Iran retaliates
events.description: Iran launches 500+ ballistic/naval missiles and ~2,000 drones. 40% aimed at Israel, 60% at US regional targets. Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman struck.

events.label: Hezbollah enters war
events.description: Hezbollah resumes rocket and drone attacks on Israel within 48 hours of the initial strike.

events.label: Strait of Hormuz closed
events.description: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz to foreign shipping. All major carriers suspend transits. Insurance cancelled from March 5.

events.label: Oil production drops 10M+ bpd
events.description: Kuwait, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and UAE production collectively drops by 10+ million barrels per day.

events.label: UNSC Resolution 2817
events.description: Security Council adopts resolution condemning Iran's attacks on neighbors. 13-0-2 (Russia and China abstain).

events.label: Ceasefire talks deadlocked
events.description: Iran rejects US 15-point ceasefire proposal as 'maximalist.' Issues counterproposal demanding reparations and sovereignty over Hormuz.

events.label: Houthis enter war
events.description: Houthis launch ballistic missiles at Israel and declare entry into the war, demanding strikes on Iran and Hezbollah stop.

events.label: April 6 deadline passes
events.description: Trump's deadline for Iran to accept ceasefire terms expires. Pakistan offers two-phased truce proposal. No deal reached.

events.label: US-Iran ceasefire agreed
events.description: Two-week ceasefire agreed via Pakistan mediation. Terms include Hormuz reopening, nuclear talks, and Iran's 10-point plan as negotiation basis.

events.label: Israel attacks Lebanon
events.description: Israel launches 'Operation Eternal Darkness' across Lebanon hours after ceasefire. 100 airstrikes in 10 minutes, 357 killed. Lebanon's inclusion in ceasefire disputed.

events.label: Hormuz remains closed
events.description: Despite ceasefire terms, Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed. Iran charges $1M+ transit tolls per vessel and limits passage.

events.label: US-Iran talks in Islamabad
events.description: Historic direct negotiations: VP Vance, Witkoff, and Kushner meet Iran's Araghchi and Ghalibaf in Pakistan. Marathon 21-hour session.

events.label: Pakistan talks collapse
events.description: Negotiations fail. Iran refuses to commit to forgoing nuclear weapons. Trump threatens full naval blockade on Iran.
events.source: NPR, Al Jazeera, Times of Israel

events.label: US naval blockade takes effect
events.description: US Navy blockade of Iran begins at 10am ET under Adm. Brad Cooper at CENTCOM. All ships entering or leaving the Strait of Hormuz require US Navy approval. Vessels that paid Iranian tolls are subject to interdiction.
events.source: CBS News, Axios, Wikipedia (2026 US naval blockade of Iran)

events.label: Brief Hormuz reopening
events.description: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open to shipping; US blockade still active. During a brief window where both sides claim the strait is open, six cruise ships transit from the Persian Gulf into the Arabian Sea. Iran disputes US framing of any new agreement.

events.label: Iran re-closes Hormuz
events.description: Iran shuts the Strait of Hormuz again, blaming US 'breaches of trust' during the ongoing ceasefire and the continued naval blockade.

events.label: Iran formalizes toll regime
events.description: Iranian parliament moves to formalize a law banning ships from 'hostile' countries from transiting the strait and imposing tolls on all others. Oil prices jump after US and Iran trade fire on commercial ships.

events.label: Trump extends ceasefire, Islamabad-2 dies
events.description: Hours before the April 22 expiration, Trump extends the two-week ceasefire at Pakistan's request to give Tehran time for a 'unified proposal.' Vance-led second Islamabad round dissolves after Iran refuses to attend. Naval blockade continues regardless of extension.
events.source: TIME, Euronews, NBC News, North Denver Tribune

events.label: Iran seizes ships in Hormuz
events.description: Hours after ceasefire extension, IRGC seizes Italian-owned MSC Francesca and the Epaminondas in the Strait of Hormuz after firing on three commercial vessels. Iran cites US capture of an Iranian commercial vessel as justification. Panama denounces seizure as 'grave attack against maritime security.'
events.source: NPR, CNBC, Washington Post, Al Jazeera

events.label: Trump 'shoot and kill' order
events.description: Trump orders US Navy to 'shoot and kill' any Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz and expands blockade scope: no ship may enter or leave the strait without US Navy approval. Brent crude tops $105/bbl on the escalation.

events.label: Hormuz reopen consensus shifts to H2 2026
events.description: Dallas Fed Energy survey: ~80% of oil and gas executives expect the Strait of Hormuz will not fully reopen until August 2026 or later. Baker Hughes concurs. IEA characterizes the closure as the 'largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market.' Brent ~$106, WTI ~$96.

events.label: Project Freedom launched
events.description: President Trump launches 'Project Freedom,' a US naval operation to escort commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. Immediate military exchanges occur, including Iranian missile/drone attacks and retaliatory US strikes on Iranian vessels.

events.label: Project Freedom paused for talks
events.description: The US temporarily pauses the 'Project Freedom' escort mission to facilitate ongoing peace negotiations mediated by Pakistan. The waterway remains blocked to standard traffic.

events.label: Negotiations progress, oil surges
events.description: Trump signals 'great progress' toward a potential agreement but warns of higher-level military strikes if negotiations fail. France and the UK work on a multinational initiative to ensure maritime security. Brent crude exceeds $113/bbl due to the volatile environment.

events.label: EU expands navigation sanctions
events.description: The EU Council formally expands its sanctions framework targeting individuals and entities obstructing freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, imposing travel bans and asset freezes.

events.label: Pakistan Army Chief in Tehran
events.description: Pakistan's Army Chief, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, arrives in Tehran for high-level, indirect peace negotiations to resolve the Strait of Hormuz crisis and nuclear dispute.

events.label: 97 ships redirected in blockade
events.description: CENTCOM reports U.S. naval forces have redirected 97 commercial vessels and disabled four others since the blockade began on April 13. Secretary Rubio notes 'some slight progress' in mediation.
events.source: CBS News, Fox News, Hamer Intel

events.label: House votes to halt the war
events.description: US House passes 215–208 a measure requiring the administration to cease operations against Iran or obtain congressional authorization to continue.

events.label: Islamabad MoU signed
events.description: Trump (Versailles) and Pezeshkian (Tehran) remotely sign a 14-point memorandum: 60-day halt in strikes, Hormuz reopened toll-free, US blockade of Iranian ports to end, oil-sanctions waiver. Nuclear, missiles, and proxies deferred to a final deal. Mojtaba Khamenei endorses with misgivings.

events.label: US lifts Iran blockade
events.description: CENTCOM announces the naval blockade of Iranian ports is lifted. Pakistan says Iran will reopen Hormuz 'instantly' and the American blockade will end 'immediately.'

events.label: Iran re-closes Hormuz over Lebanon
events.description: One day after Trump announces an Israel–Hezbollah ceasefire, Iran shuts Hormuz again, citing continued Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon as a MoU violation. The US military denies the claim.
events.source: Reuters / Al Arabiya, 20 June 2026; Al Jazeera

events.label: Senate votes to halt the war
events.description: US Senate passes 50–48 a measure mandating an end to war operations or congressional consent to continue — the second chamber to rebuke the campaign.

events.label: MoU stress-tested in Hormuz
events.description: After the M/V Ever Lovely and tanker MT Kiku are hit in the strait, US jets strike Iranian missile, drone, and radar sites on Qeshm and along Hormuz. IRGC hits US-linked targets in Bahrain and Kuwait. Each side accuses the other of violating the June deal.
events.source: NYT, 27 June 2026; NBC News, 28 June 2026; CENTCOM

events.label: Trump declares MoU 'over'
events.description: After Iranian attacks on commercial ships asserting sovereignty over Hormuz, Trump says the memorandum is 'over' and 'I don't want to deal with them anymore.' US strike packages that week hit ≥170 targets — about 17 times the 26 June salvo.
events.source: Wikipedia (Islamabad Memorandum); CBS News, 10 July 2026; Reuters

events.label: US reimposes naval blockade
events.description: CENTCOM reimposes the naval blockade of Iranian ports at 16:00 ET, reversing the 18 June lift that was the centrepiece of the MoU.

events.label: Thirteen nights of strikes, then a pause
events.description: After 13 consecutive nights of US strikes and Iranian retaliatory attacks on Gulf bases, Trump says he is close to deciding on a 'massive attack,' then both sides pause direct strikes. US officials later describe extreme interceptor shortages.

events.label: Iran strikes US forces in Jordan
events.description: Iran conducts a ballistic-missile attack on US forces in Jordan. Washington calls it an 'attempted surprise attack' and resumes strikes on 29–30 July, ending the four-day pause.

events.label: Dual-lane Hormuz framework, never starts
events.description: Tehran approves a dual-lane transit framework with Oman — zero tolls, mine clearance of the main lane within 30 days — on a separate 60-day clock. Clearance rallies; the mine work never starts.
events.source: Kpler, 19 August 2026; Crisis Group trigger list

events.label: 60-day MoU window lapses
events.description: The Islamabad Memorandum's deadline for a final deal passes with no agreement, no extension, and no talks under way. Araghchi says Tehran 'never had a ceasefire that would now need to be extended.' Trump answers 'No' when asked about an extension.

events.label: UAE severs Iran; Ghalibaf keeps Hormuz shut
events.description: After reporting two Iranian missiles, one landing in its territorial waters, the UAE suspends all trade, exchange, and financial transactions with Iran. Ghalibaf tells lawmakers Hormuz stays shut until the blockade is lifted, frozen assets released, and oil sanctions removed. Iran denies the missile claim.
events.source: Forbes, 18 August 2026; Reuters; Wikipedia (2026 Iran war)

events.label: Trump declares 'Economic D-Day'
events.description: Trump announces that any country trading with Iran will be sanctioned, branding the package 'Economic D-Day.' A US official says the IRGC 'doesn't control the strait. We do.' Hormuz crossings print as low as 7 per day against a pre-war ~130.
events.source: Times of Israel, 22 August 2026; Reuters, 19 August 2026; Kpler
